name: Liverpool 2004/05
scopeNote: Liverpool under Rafael Benítez (rafael-benitez), 2004/05: Champions League winners (Istanbul, 25 May 2005), fifth in the Premier League, League Cup runners-up, FA Cup out in round 3. Period runs from the Champions League third qualifying round first leg at Grazer AK (10 August 2004, date from a search summary only, see openQuestions) to the final. Style as sources name it: 4-2-3-1 in the final, 4-4-2 for Baroš and Cissé (Benítez), 5-3-1-1 vs Juventus, two banks of four vs Chelsea, zonal marking at set pieces with rotation. A 4-4-1-1 label was not found for Liverpool in any read page (the only 4-4-1-1 in the Spanish Coaches' Voice page is Milan's defensive shape). Most tactical coverage of the league season is retrospective; the Istanbul final and the Chelsea tie are the best-documented matches.
openQuestions: Start date 2004-08-10 (Grazer AK 0-2 Liverpool) comes from a search summary only; confirm on LFChistory game 4903 or UEFA.
Istanbul half-time shape: Coaches' Voice says 3-4-2-1, Sky Sports says 3-5-2; Benítez's Dec 2019 account is three at the back with Hamann in midfield.
Starting shape in the final is called 4-2-3-1 (Coaches' Voice) but other pages (not mined) say 4-4-1-1; Kewell behind Baroš per Sky.

No contemporary (2004/05) tactical source found for build-up, pressing intensity, or the man-marking inside the zonal scheme (a review of Benítez's book claims the zonal system was often altered to man-mark individual players; not read).
Set-piece preparation for Chelsea/Juventus ties not found; Tomkins Times set-piece pieces were not accessible.
Squad age not found with a source.

sources.title: AC Milan 3 Liverpool 3: Classic Matches - Coaches' Voice
sources.evidence: Liverpool were organised by their manager Rafa Benítez into a 4-2-3-1 formation in which Steven Gerrard and Xabi Alonso started in central midfield.

sources.title: AC Milan 3 Liverpool 3: Classic Matches - Coaches' Voice
sources.evidence: Benítez changed their structure at half-time to a 3-4-2-1. The scoreline, and injuries to Harry Kewell – who had been replaced early by Vladimir Smicer – and later Steve Finnan forced the Spaniard to do so, and with Dietmar Hamann introduced as an additional midfielder, there was an immediate change in the style and confidence of their play.

sources.title: AC Milan 3 Liverpool 3: Classic Matches - Coaches' Voice
sources.evidence: Liverpool were sluggish and uninspiring in possession. Luis García drifted infield from his position wide on the right, but would have been more effective maintaining their attacking width. Milan’s central press also frustrated Liverpool in midfield, making it difficult for them to build possession.
